title: The Minimum Catering Spend Tested Against When an Agreement Closes
content:
The minimum tested against when a Corporate Catering Service Agreement closes is read down where the client also runs a cafe with Larkspur Table, because catering bought through the cafe kitchen is programme spend by another name.

| How long the agreement has run | The client's Workplace Cafe Management Program contract at the agreement's delivery site | The minimum tested against |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 24 months (two years) or more | stands active, and its service model permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen | three quarters — 0.75, that is 75 per cent — of the minimum annual catering spend printed against the catering service level |
| At least 12 months (a year) and fewer than 24 months | stands active | seven eighths — 0.875, that is 87.5 per cent — of the minimum annual catering spend printed against the catering service level |
| Any other case | — | the minimum annual catering spend printed against the catering service level |

**The first row asks for both conditions together.** An agreement that has run 30 months at a site where the client's cafe contract stands active but whose service model does not permit catering to be ordered out of that kitchen does not meet the first row; nor does an agreement of 30 months at a site where the client holds no cafe contract at all.

**The second row asks only that the cafe contract stands active.** What its service model permits is not tested there, but the age of the agreement is: 12 months or more and fewer than 24.

**A contract that does not stand active answers neither row.** Both rows are written for a contract standing active at the agreement's delivery site, so a contract in any other standing leaves the agreement on the last row.

**Illustration on hypothetical figures.** Where the minimum annual catering spend printed against the catering service level is 42000.00 USD: an agreement of 26 months whose cafe contract at the delivery site stands active and whose service model permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen is tested against 31500.00 USD; an agreement of 18 months whose cafe contract at that site stands active is tested against 36750.00 USD; an agreement of 8 months, or one at a site with no cafe contract standing active, is tested against 42000.00 USD.

The site tested is the delivery site written on the catering agreement, and the two facts read off the Workplace Cafe Management Program contract at that site are whether it stands active and whether catering may be ordered out of that cafe kitchen.
